target.title: Add shareable subscription usage cards
target.body:
## Product case

CodexBar already computes local token and estimated-cost history, but the menu is a poor sharing surface: the numbers cannot be copied as one artifact, and a menu screenshot is fragile and difficult to read. This PR turns the existing local data into a fixed 1200x630 card plus a plain-text equivalent.

The intentionally narrow v1 is **local export**, not a hosted profile:

- no account system, public URL, upload, tracking, or backend;
- no prompt, project, path, email, or account identity in the payload;
- no attempt to make unlike measurements look complete; unknown spend remains unknown;
- one immutable payload drives preview, PNG, clipboard text, and saved image.

Alternatives considered:

- **Screenshot the current menu:** clips, changes size, and mixes controls with the artifact.
- **Hosted share link / OG page:** introduces persistence, deletion, abuse, and privacy-policy work that is not justified for v1.
- **Provider-by-provider exports:** fails the core use case of comparing all enabled AI subscriptions in one picture.

## What this adds

- A native **Share Stats...** action in the status menu and Settings -> Menu -> Sharing.
- A 1200x630 local card with combined 30-day tracked tokens and estimated spend.
- Distinct ranked subscription rows with readable inline plan names and a three-model ranking.
- A ten-bucket activity strip whose colors reinforce the named subscription rows.
- OpenRouter API-key spend surfaced as explicitly labeled month-to-date data rather than hidden or mixed into the trailing-period total.
- **Copy Image**, **Copy Stats**, and **Save...** actions from one preview.
- Existing CodexBar typography, localization patterns, menu descriptors, and lifecycle handling.

## Permission and prompt boundary

The feature adds no entitlement, system permission request, network request, background upload, or automatic pasteboard write.

| User action | Side effect |
| --- | --- |
| Open Share Stats | Reads in-memory provider snapshots and configured local Codex history only. No prompt is presented. |
| Copy Image | Writes PNG/TIFF data to the pasteboard after the explicit button press. |
| Copy Stats | Writes plain text to the pasteboard after the explicit button press. |
| Save... | Presents the standard save panel only after the explicit button press. |

Sibling Codex-account history uses the account homes already represented in CodexBar settings. A missing, unreadable, or timed-out history source degrades to an unpriced connected row; the sharing flow does not request broad filesystem access to compensate.

## Account-complete data contract

| Surface | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Tracked tokens | Sum of known local token-history snapshots in the selected 30-day window. |
| Estimated spend | Sum of finite priced history only; the card reports priced-source coverage. |
| Codex subscriptions | One identity-free row per visible Codex account, labeled `Codex · #1`, `Codex · #2`, etc. |
| Other subscriptions | One row per enabled provider source. Missing local history reads `connected`, never `$0`. |
| OpenRouter spend | Uses the existing in-memory `keyUsageMonthly` value, labels it `MTD`, and reports it separately from trailing-30-day totals. |
| Top models | Cross-provider aggregation of real model breakdowns or model names for the same window; each row names its provider. |
| Activity strip | Tracked tokens grouped into at most ten time buckets and stacked by named subscription. |

The active Codex account reuses the normal provider snapshot. Each sibling account scans its own Codex home into a separate hashed cache, with Pi session history disabled for sibling scans so shared Pi history is counted exactly once. Account scan failures degrade to connected/unpriced rows rather than deleting a visible subscription.

## Readability and accessibility

- The card is designed and checked at its 600 x 315 feed render, not only at the 1200 x 630 export size.
- Essential labels start at 18 pt native; subscription and model names use 20 pt. Tiny plan pills and model-mapping microcopy were removed.
- Every provider and model association uses a name and two-digit rank in addition to a compact color locator.
- Against the warm near-black background, primary text measures 16.5:1, secondary text 8.1:1, and the OpenRouter accent 7.8:1.
- The exported artifact is static and does not depend on motion or hover state.
- The sourced standards, Exa/Parallel comparison, and OpenRouter frontier-model panel are documented in [the readability review](docs/share-card-readability-review-2026-07-13.md).

## Privacy allowlist

The export payload permits provider display name, plan label, aggregate tokens, aggregate estimated cost, active-day counts, model name, period end, and per-subscription daily aggregate token counts. It does not carry email, account ID, project name/path, prompt text, session title, file content, credentials, or raw event records. Rendering and pasteboard/save operations are local.

## Current configured-bundle proof

These images come from a freshly compiled, signed local app bundle using the contributor's real configured aggregate data. The payload contains no account identity, prompts, projects, paths, endpoints, or credentials.

![Current real-bundle share card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/codex/shareable-usage-card/docs/screenshots/share-stats-real-bundle.png)

![Current real-bundle preview after Copy Image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/codex/shareable-usage-card/docs/screenshots/share-stats-real-preview.png)

Observed behavior:

- The production preview surfaced four named subscriptions, three named models, a 30-day estimate, and a separate OpenRouter MTD figure.
- Clicking the preview's real **Copy Image** action produced a 1200 x 630 pasteboard item with `public.png` and `public.tiff` representations; the preview status changed to `Image copied`.
- Clicking **Copy Stats** produced 610 characters containing the live subscription names, model-provider mappings, OpenRouter MTD amount, and local-generation provenance.
- No screen-recording permission was granted or required. The proof image was recovered from CodexBar's own clipboard export path.

## Relationship to the Settings dashboard

- Companion PR: [#2116 - Settings: add unified usage and spend dashboard](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2116)
- This PR owns the share/export workflow only.
- #2116 owns persistent in-app exploration only.
- Neither branch depends on the other at build or runtime.

## Verification

- [x] Incremental arm64 release build after the feed-readability redesign
- [x] Exact 1200 x 630 production view exported and visually inspected at both native and 600 x 315 feed size
- [x] Real configured-bundle Copy Image and Copy Stats paths exercised through the preview controls
- [x] Primary, secondary, and accent contrast measured at 16.5:1, 8.1:1, and 7.8:1
- [x] No new entitlement, dependency, network path, or automatic pasteboard behavior
- [ ] Real configured-bundle Save... confirmation
- [x] `swift test --filter ShareStatsTests` - 8 focused tests passed
- [x] `make check` - localization, formatting, SwiftLint, shell/docs/package gates passed
- [x] Fresh sharded test suite in GitHub CI

The local widget-packaging step is blocked by an installed Xcode `IDESimulatorFoundation` / `DVTDownloads` plug-in mismatch. This is machine-local; the CodexBar target builds cleanly, and GitHub CI is the authoritative full-suite result. The focused share-stat suite passes locally, including privacy-label and shared-calendar-window regressions. GitHub CI remains the authoritative full-suite result.

## Product/design decision requested

`VISION.md` requires sign-off for new product surfaces. This PR asks maintainers to approve a permanent, privacy-first local usage-card export that includes every visible subscription without exposing account identity or adding permission prompts.

target.title: Block background Chromium Keychain access
target.body:
## Summary

- block Chromium browser-cookie imports during background provider refreshes
- preserve browser-cookie access for user-initiated refreshes and the existing Keychain pre-alert flow
- update gate tests to prove background paths do not even perform the Keychain preflight

## Root cause

Chromium cookie decryption reads `Chrome Safe Storage` from Keychain. The previous background path could proceed into the browser importer whenever an attribute-only preflight appeared allowed, even though the later password-data read could require user interaction.

## Impact

Automatic refreshes no longer initiate the Chromium Keychain path. A user-initiated refresh remains the consent boundary for browser-cookie authentication.

## Validation

- targeted test changes use `KeychainAccessPreflight` test overrides and do not touch a real Keychain item
- `git diff --check`
- the full local SwiftPM test executable was blocked by unrelated auxiliary-target timestamp churn after the modified core module compiled; this is recorded rather than treated as a passing test

## Follow-up

SweetCookieKit is being hardened separately so no host can implicitly promote a no-UI Safe Storage read to an interactive one. Once released, CodexBar should bump that dependency.

Fixes #2213
Related: #2214

target.title: Add high-contrast mode for inactive displays
target.body: ## Summary - add an opt-in **Improve visibility on inactive displays** toggle under Settings > Menu Bar for the **Icon & percent** style - render the status item image and metric as a single attributed title with `NSTextAttachment` when enabled - disable the control for other icon styles and gate the effective renderer to Icon & percent while preserving the stored preference when switching styles - keep the existing AppKit image/title path as the default and restore it immediately when the toggle is disabled - persist the setting, localize it across all 23 supported locales, and cover the settings/rendering paths with tests ## Context On multi-display macOS setups, AppKit dims standard `NSStatusBarButton` image/title content quite aggressively on inactive displays. A three-display comparison on macOS 26.5.2 showed that template images embedded in an attributed title remain significantly more legible. macOS still applies some system-level inactive-display dimming, so this is an opt-in readability improvement rather than a promise that applications can force an absolutely identical active/inactive appearance. The scope is intentionally limited to **Icon & percent**, which is the renderer covered by the live visual proof below. See #2190 for the original user screenshot and request. ## Visual proof Tested from a freshly built bundle at `b3a64eb` (CodexBar `0.43.1 (105)`) on macOS `26.5.2 (25F84)` with three extended displays and mirroring disabled. ### Active/inactive displays, Dark/Light appearances, toggle off/on The matching inactive-display crops show median non-background pixel luminance increasing from about 35 to 115 in Dark appearance and from about 34 to 113 in Light appearance (roughly 3.3×). The active-display appearance remains visually unchanged. ### Menu-open/highlighted and toggle-off restoration Top: the status item is highlighted with its menu open. Bottom: the same inactive display with high contrast **off** (left, native dimming restored) and then **on again** (right, readability restored). The captures are cropped to the menu bar and CodexBar card only. ### Warning-flash compatibility This side-by-side artifact was rendered through the production `quotaWarningFlashImage` and `highContrastButtonTitle` methods using the real Codex brand asset. The one-off export harness was removed after capture and is not part of the patch. The live setting was restored to **enabled** after the off/on check. No real quota notification was manufactured; the warning path was exercised through the production renderer and focused automated tests instead. ## Validation - merged current `main` into the PR branch and resolved the changelog conflict without rebasing or force-pushing - `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer make check` passed (SwiftFormat clean; SwiftLint: 0 violations in 1450 files) - focused post-merge tests: 41/41 passed across `PreferencesPaneSmokeTests`, `StatusItemAnimationSignatureTests`, and `StatusItemQuotaWarningFlashTests` - the focused coverage now verifies that the preference is available only for Icon & percent, switching to Critters uses the native renderer, and switching back restores the stored high-contrast behavior - `make test` stopped after retrying one unrelated, environment-dependent existing test: `browser uninstall invalidates cookie source immediately`; on this Mac, Launch Services finds another registered Chrome installation after the test simulates uninstall, and both `BrowserDetection.swift` and `BrowserDetectionTests.swift` are identical to current `origin/main` - packaged and code-signature-verified an isolated Debug app with Keychain access and provider refreshes disabled for the original live proof - compared the toggle off/on on three extended displays in both Dark and Light appearances; the inactive-display icon and metric changed from heavily dimmed dark gray to a substantially brighter, readable rendering Closes #2190

- mirror the menu-bar app's precedence: 2+ swap accounts replace ambient/token Claude cards, while zero/one account keeps existing output
- preserve explicit account and non-auto `--source` intent, ambient fallback diagnostics, active-account state, and sentinel/no-usage rows

- keep macOS and Linux CLI coverage synchronized, including every explicit source override and active sentinel rendering

## Testing

- `swift build --target CodexBarCLI`
